decisions.reason: It extends the firm’s wafer-packaging capabilities in a growing semiconductor market and, despite uncertain uptake, still looks like a core-adjacent option worth carrying for another year.
This carrier wafer is very close to the established business, fits the firm’s thin-wafer handling direction, and is likely inexpensive to keep on offer relative to its option value.
The Cu-interposer glass wafer is technically more uncertain and costlier to develop, but it matches the firm’s move toward multifunctional packaging wafers so the option remains worth preserving.
An off-the-shelf brand for standard glass and quartz wafers is a low-cost commercial extension of the core portfolio and is therefore cheap to maintain while demand develops.

Glass-based circuit boards are the most distant from the firm’s established offer, likely require more commitment to prove value, and are the clearest candidate for reallocating resources back to core substrate and packaging projects.
